context_note: Marcillo & Miguez 2017 meta-analysis, corn only (no soybean data). The CI in the text (1.17-1.29) does not match Figure 1 (1.16-1.26); the figure is more internally consistent. No pooled RR across all cover crop types is reported. Mixed-model meta-analysis, 268 observations from 65 studies, 1965-2015.

Grass WCC effect is neutral. n=140 (47 studies) confirmed in Table 4. Grass is the largest group and the most common cover crop type (cereal rye), so it is the most representative of typical adoption.
Smallest group (n=28, 13 studies). The effect depends strongly on termination timing (see E8): early termination gives RR 0.97.

The abstract quote gives a range (30-33%) that combines low N and no-till. Assigning 33% to low N (0-99 kg N/ha) is backed by Figure 4 (RR 1.33 [1.24,1.43]). This is a subgroup result, not an average; at >200 kg N/ha the effect is null (0.98). Do not count it together with E7 as independent pooled estimates.
Legume subgroup at mid N rate; Figure 4 RR 1.09 [1.04,1.13].
Legume subgroup under no-till. Overlaps the 30% figure in the abstract sentence quoted in E4, but it is a separate subgroup (tillage, not N rate).
Mixture subgroup terminated late (0-6 days before corn). Early termination (>14 d) gives RR 0.97 [0.95,1.00]. This is a best-case subgroup.

Southeast region, all WCC types. The text says 1.12, but Figure 6 shows Southeast 1.14 [1.09,1.19]: the paper contradicts itself. The quote matches the text. North Central (Corn Belt, most observations) is only 1.03 [1.00,1.06]; Canada 1.01; Great Plains 1.00.

Northeast region, all WCC types. The text says 1.14, but Figure 6 shows 1.15 [1.09,1.21]: the text and figure disagree. E9 and E10 share the same quote but report different values, so they are not duplicates.
